subject: Physical education

source.title: National curriculum in England: physical education programmes of study

note: Controlled paraphrases of the statutory Physical Education programmes of study. Example content in square brackets is not represented as a statutory requirement. Swimming and water safety requirements are included separately because the source specifies them as a distinct requirement.

KS1.summary: Master basic running, jumping, throwing and catching movements and develop balance, agility and coordination.
Participate in team games and develop simple attacking and defending tactics.
Perform dances using simple movement patterns.

KS2.summary: Apply and combine running, jumping, throwing and catching skills and develop a broader range of movement sequences.
Play competitive games and apply basic principles for attacking and defending.
Develop flexibility, strength, technique, control and balance.
Perform dances using a range of movement patterns.
Take part in outdoor and adventurous activity challenges individually and in teams.
Compare performances with previous performances and demonstrate improvement towards a personal best.
Provide swimming instruction in KS1 or KS2 so pupils can swim at least 25 metres, use a range of strokes effectively and perform safe self-rescue in different water situations.

KS3.summary: Use tactics and strategies to overcome opponents in direct competition through team and individual games.
Develop technique and improve performance in competitive sports and physical activities.
Perform dances using advanced techniques across different dance styles and forms.
Take part in outdoor and adventurous activities that present physical and intellectual challenges and develop teamwork and problem-solving.
Analyse performance against previous performances and demonstrate improvement towards a personal best.
Take part in competitive sports and activities outside school through community links or sports clubs.

KS4.summary: Use and develop tactics and strategies to overcome opponents in team and individual games.
Develop technique and improve performance in competitive sports or other physical activities.
Take part in demanding outdoor and adventurous activities that develop teamwork, trust and problem-solving.
Evaluate performances and demonstrate improvement across physical activities towards a personal best.
Continue to take part regularly in competitive sports and activities outside school through community links or sports clubs.
Engage in complex physical activities that develop personal fitness and promote an active, healthy lifestyle.
